evals.query: Create a Kora JDBC repository for a User with an auto-generated Long id, email, name and createdAt columns. I need findById, findAll, insert and delete.
expected_behavior: Defines a record annotated with @EntityJdbc from io.koraframework.database.jdbc.annotation, plus @Table/@Column/@Id from io.koraframework.database.common.annotation
Declares a @Repository interface extending JdbcRepository with synchronous method signatures
Uses SQL macros such as %{return#selects}, %{return#table}, %{entity#inserts} in @Query
Returns @Nullable User (preferred over Optional) for findById and List<User> for findAll
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (or ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors") and a JDBC driver dependency
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, JPA @Entity, reflection-based ORM annotations, or field injection

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 service compiles fine but dies at startup with 'ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: ROOT.jdbc.username'. My application.conf has a db { } block with jdbcUrl, username and password, and nothing under jdbc.
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as the 1.x section name: the config section was renamed from db to jdbc in Kora 2.0
States that JdbcDatabaseModule wires new JdbcDatabaseFactoryModule("jdbc"), so the path in the message is the one Kora looks for, not one the file contains
Renames the whole block to jdbc { } rather than adding a jdbc.username key next to db
Notes that the stale db { } block is an unrecognised HOCON section, ignored without a warning, which is why the build stayed green
Does not suggest a namingStrategy, a config-mapper change, or renaming JdbcDatabaseConfig fields

evals.query: I renamed db to jdbc in every .conf file for the Kora 2.0 migration, but one @KoraAppTest still fails with 'Config expected value, but got null at path: ROOT.jdbc.username'. The resource files are definitely migrated.
expected_behavior: Points at HOCON embedded in test sources via KoraConfigModification.ofString("""...""")
Explains that inline test HOCON carries the same keys and is missed by scans that only read .conf and .yaml files
Applies the same rename inside the ofString block: jdbc { jdbcUrl, username, password, poolName }
Mentions KoraConfigModification.ofSystemProperty / withSystemProperty as the other test config entry points
Does not conclude the resource files are still wrong when they have already been migrated

evals.query: Porting a repository to Kora 2.0: I changed every import from ru.tinkoff.kora to io.koraframework and now javac says 'cannot find symbol: class EntityJdbc' for io.koraframework.database.jdbc.EntityJdbc. @Repository, @Query and @Column resolve fine.
expected_behavior: States that @EntityJdbc moved to io.koraframework.database.jdbc.annotation.EntityJdbc in Kora 2.0
Notes that it is the only database annotation whose package changed — @Repository, @Query, @Id, @Table, @Column, @Embedded and @Batch stay in io.koraframework.database.common.annotation
Warns against applying one blanket package-rewrite rule to every database annotation and recommends checking each import
Does not suggest that @EntityJdbc was removed or replaced by another annotation

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0. KSP fails with 'Suspend methods are not supported by the repository generator' on my PetRepository. Can I just drop the suspend keyword from the repository interface?
expected_behavior: Confirms repository contracts are synchronous in Kora 2.0 and that suspend, Mono, Flux and CompletionStage repository methods were all removed
States that dropping suspend is not a mechanical keyword deletion: it propagates up through services, controllers and tests

Names the behavioural consequences: coroutine cancellation no longer cancels the database call, transaction boundaries are now the inTx lambda rather than a coroutine context, and exceptions propagate as ordinary throws
Says the runTest/runBlocking wrappers around the now-synchronous calls should be removed, and kotlinx-coroutines dependencies dropped once the last coroutine usage is gone
Mentions that a suspend repository kept only as a duplicate of an existing synchronous one should be deleted outright rather than converted into a second interface
Points at Java StructuredTaskScope (preview, --enable-preview) for real parallel fan-out instead of keeping a coroutine bridge
Does not suggest wrapping the repository call in withContext(Dispatchers.IO) to keep the suspend signature

evals.query: Migrating a Kora service to 2.0: repository.getJdbcConnectionFactory().inTx(...) no longer compiles, and JdbcConnectionFactory cannot be resolved either. What replaces it?
expected_behavior: States that JdbcRepository now exposes executor() returning JdbcExecutor from io.koraframework.database.jdbc
Shows repository.executor().inTx(...) as the replacement and notes JdbcExecutor can also be injected directly into a @Component
Mentions that the graph implementation is JdbcDataSource, so no JdbcDatabase or JdbcConnectionFactory component exists any more
Maps currentConnectionContext() to currentContext() and the post-action methods to ConnectionContext.afterCommit / afterRollback if those appear
Does not invent a JdbcConnectionFactory replacement class or suggest injecting javax.sql.DataSource and managing transactions by hand

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0. repository.executor().inTx { repository.insert(entity); entity } fails with 'Cannot infer type for type parameter T'. The same code shape worked before the migration.
expected_behavior: Explains that inTx now has several overloads (SqlSupplier, SqlRunnable, SqlFunction<ConnectionContext,T>, SqlConsumer, each with and without a TxIsolation) so Kotlin cannot pick one from a bare lambda
Gives the fix as an explicit SAM constructor: inTx(JdbcExecutor.SqlSupplier { ... }) when a value is returned and inTx(JdbcExecutor.SqlRunnable { ... }) when nothing is
Notes that the error text (or 'Overload resolution ambiguity') never mentions transactions, which is why it is easy to misdiagnose
Notes that Java infers correctly from a bare lambda, so only Kotlin call sites need changing
Does not suggest casting the lambda, adding explicit type arguments to inTx, or restructuring the transaction to avoid the problem

evals.query: Kotlin, Kora 2.0. My column mapper 'class TaskStatusParameterMapper : JdbcParameterColumnMapper<TaskStatus> { override fun set(stmt: PreparedStatement, index: Int, value: TaskStatus) { ... } }' fails with "'set' overrides nothing". The Java version of the same mapper in another module compiles.
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as nullability: the 2.0 mapper contracts are JSpecify-marked, so the value parameter must be declared TaskStatus?
Shows the corrected signature: override fun set(stmt: PreparedStatement, index: Int, value: TaskStatus?)
Notes the same applies to JdbcResultColumnMapper.apply(rs, index) and JdbcRowMapper.apply(row), and that return types may still be narrowed to non-null
Explains the Java/Kotlin asymmetry: Java does not enforce the annotation, which is why the Java twin compiles
Points out that the error message never mentions nullability
Does not suggest changing the generic type argument to TaskStatus? or adding @JvmSuppressWildcards / a platform-type cast

evals.query: Kora 2.0. One of my JDBC mappers fails the graph build with 'No component found for dependency: JdbcResultColumnMapper<Status>' and another with 'Multiple components match dependency'. Should every mapper just be a @Component?
expected_behavior: Answers no, and ties the decision to the mapper's own shape rather than a blanket rule
States that a @Mapping-named mapper that is final (Kotlin: not open) with a public no-arg constructor and no @Tag is instantiated by the generated repository itself and needs no @Component
States that a mapper with constructor dependencies, a non-final Java class, or a @Tag is injected as a constructor parameter of the generated repository and therefore must be a @Component
States that a field or parameter with no @Mapping resolves its mapper from the graph by type, so that mapper must be a @Component and only one component may produce that type
Maps each error to its cause: 'No component found' means an injected mapper is missing from the graph, 'Multiple components match' means two components produce the same mapper type
Does not recommend annotating every mapper with @Component, and does not suggest @Tag as the default fix

evals.query: We are on Kora 2.0 and want non-blocking database access. Should we move our repositories from database-jdbc to database-r2dbc, or to the Vert.x SQL module?
expected_behavior: States plainly that database-r2dbc and database-vertx do not exist in Kora 2.0 — they were removed, and there is no reactive database module to migrate to
Explains the 2.0 execution model: contracts are synchronous and blocking JDBC runs on virtual threads, so a reactive driver is not the lever it used to be
Recommends staying on database-jdbc and sizing the Hikari pool as the real concurrency limit
Does not invent a replacement artifact, suggest wrapping repositories in CompletableFuture/Mono to simulate reactivity, or point at kora-docs pages for r2dbc/vertx (those document 1.x)

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 repository the query @Query("DELETE FROM %{entity#table} WHERE id = :id") UpdateCount deleteById(Long id) fails the build with 'Query macro target entity cannot be resolved'. The entity is annotated with @EntityJdbc and @Table.
expected_behavior: Explains that a macro target must resolve within the annotated method: a parameter name, return, a nested path, or a type parameter of the repository
Points out that deleteById(Long id) has no parameter called entity, so %{entity#table} cannot resolve regardless of the entity's annotations
Fixes it by naming the table literally, or by targeting the repository's type parameter (%{V#table}) in a generic base interface
Lists the real 2.0 macro command set — table, table as alias, selects, columns, values, inserts, updates, where — and notes there is no deletes command
Does not invent a %{entity#deletes} macro or claim @Table is missing

evals.query: How do I insert a row and get back the database-generated identity id in a Kora 2.0 JDBC repository?
expected_behavior: Annotates the insert method with @Id and returns the id type (e.g. Long), or projects it with an explicit RETURNING id clause
Excludes the id column from the INSERT with %{entity#inserts -= @id}
Notes that @Id-on-method also works with @Batch, returning List<Long> in input order
Does not invent a @GeneratedValue annotation or a %{entity#deletes} macro

evals.query: Write a Kora 2.0 service that inserts an order and reserves inventory atomically, sending a notification only after the transaction commits.
expected_behavior: Runs the work inside repository.executor().inTx(...), or through an injected JdbcExecutor
Calls multiple repository methods inside the same inTx lambda so they share one transaction and roll back together
Registers the notification with ConnectionContext.afterCommit(...), taking the context from the inTx overload that supplies it rather than the nullable currentContext()
Declares the service as a @Component with constructor injection
Does not use @Transactional, declarative propagation, getJdbcConnectionFactory(), or addPostCommitAction

evals.query: Add bulk insert and update methods to my Kora 2.0 JDBC UserRepository.
expected_behavior: Annotates the List<User> parameter with @Batch (the annotation targets the parameter, not the method)
Returns UpdateCount, void, int[]/long[], or generated ids with @Id — not an arbitrary projection of rows
Uses %{entity#inserts} / %{entity#updates} macros in @Query
Does not call PreparedStatement.addBatch by hand or reach for a JdbcTemplate-style helper

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 entity has a Status enum stored as an integer code column. How do I map it both ways, in Java and in Kotlin?
expected_behavior: Implements JdbcResultColumnMapper<Status> with apply(ResultSet rs, int index) to read the code
Implements JdbcParameterColumnMapper<Status> with set(PreparedStatement, int, value) to write it, handling null via setNull
Selects both by repeating @Mapping on the field — the annotation is @Repeatable, there is no array attribute form
In Kotlin declares the mapper parameter as Status? and uses @field: for @Id/@Column while applying @Mapping without a use-site target
Decides @Component correctly: a final/no-arg mapper named by @Mapping is constructed by the generated repository and needs none
Does not use a JPA AttributeConverter or an external converter framework

evals.query: I have an order_items table with a composite primary key (order_id, product_id). How do I model it in Kora 2.0 JDBC?
expected_behavior: Models the key as a nested record/data class referenced with @Id @Embedded on the parent entity field (Kotlin: @field:Id @field:Embedded)
Uses %{id#where} in findById/deleteById and %{entity#where = @id} when the method takes the entity
Keeps @EntityJdbc on the parent entity and notes the nested key type does not need it
Targets the key columns in ON CONFLICT with %{entity#selects = @id} rather than hardcoding them
Does not use JPA @IdClass or @EmbeddedId

evals.query: How do I persist a nested record into a PostgreSQL jsonb column with Kora 2.0 JDBC?
expected_behavior: Annotates the field and the payload type with @Json from io.koraframework.json.common.annotation
Declares a small @Module with generic @Json-tagged JdbcParameterColumnMapper<T> / JdbcResultColumnMapper<T> factories depending on JsonWriter<T> / JsonReader<T>
Explains that the @Json tag is what keeps the generic factory from matching every unsupported column type in the graph
Casts the parameter in SQL, e.g. VALUES (:entity.id, :entity.value::jsonb)
Wires io.koraframework.json.common.JsonModule (artifact json-common) into the @KoraApp graph
Uses writer.toString(value) and reader.read(value) — the *Unchecked variants were removed in 2.0 and the plain methods no longer throw checked exceptions
Does not use Jackson ObjectMapper directly or reference JsonCommonModule / the json-module artifact

evals.query: Configure the HikariCP connection pool for a Kora 2.0 JDBC service with credentials from environment variables, a 20-connection pool, and query metrics and logs visible in observability.
expected_behavior: Places jdbcUrl, username, password, poolName and maxPoolSize under the jdbc section (not db) read by JdbcDatabaseConfig
Enables telemetry.logging.enabled and telemetry.metrics.enabled explicitly, noting both default to false in Kora 2.0
Uses HOCON duration strings like connectionTimeout = "10s" rather than millisecond numbers
Substitutes credentials with environment variables (${POSTGRES_JDBC_URL}, ${POSTGRES_USER}, ${POSTGRES_PASS})
Wires JdbcDatabaseModule and a config module (HoconConfigModule) into @KoraApp, plus a metrics module for the registry
Does not build a DataSource by hand or use raw Hikari property names as top-level keys

evals.query: Kora 2.0 build fails with 'SQL query placeholder has no matching method parameter: :id / Available parameters: - :arg0'. My repository method is findById(Long id) and the parameter really is called id. A clean rebuild in a colleague's checkout works.
expected_behavior: Identifies :arg0 as the tell that the processor read the repository interface from a compiled class file with synthetic parameter names, not from the source
Attributes it to an incremental/cached build rather than to the query or the method signature
Fixes it with ./gradlew clean or --rerun-tasks
Does not suggest renaming parameters to arg0, switching to positional placeholders, or adding -parameters as the fix
Mentions the related case where phantom ru.tinkoff.kora errors come from stale sources under build/generated, and that generated code must never be hand-edited

evals.query: How should I write an integration test for a Kora 2.0 JDBC repository against a real PostgreSQL?
expected_behavior: Uses @KoraAppTest with io.koraframework:test-junit5 and injects the repository with @TestComponent
Starts PostgreSQL via Testcontainers and points the config at it through KoraConfigModification (ofSystemProperty/withSystemProperty, or ofString for an inline jdbc { } block)
Uses the jdbc section name in any inline test HOCON
Exercises the real generated repository implementation rather than instantiating or mocking it
Does not use a boot-test annotation from another framework, a JPA slice test, or mock the repository
